result.title: Look Before You Restore: Learning to Predict Before Acting for Agentic Image Restoration
result.summary: Agents for mixed-degradation image restoration typically learn what a tool does to an image only after running it: failed calls waste computation and harmful outputs go unnoticed until too late. We propose PreActIR, an agentic restoration framework that predicts tool consequences before execution. For each candidate tool, a tool-conditioned world model forecasts changes in residual degradation, image quality, and fidelity, together with the risk of harm and the uncertainty of the prediction. The agent executes the top-ranked candidate, and an independent verifier commits or rolls back its output before the agent replans from the observed state. PreActIR also audits whether performance is limited by the selector or by the candidate space, and studies targeted tool adaptation as a controlled way to expand that space. In a controlled evaluation that fixes the candidate pool, verifier, and budget and employs reference-annotated degradation states, PreActIR uses 42.5% fewer real tool calls and 63.4% fewer rejected calls than reactive, execute-then-evaluate trial and error, while improving Y-PSNR by 0.92 dB.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PreActIR：一个混合退化图像复原的 agent 框架，用工具条件化的 world model 在执行前预测候选工具对残差退化、画质与保真度的影响及风险与不确定性，由独立 verifier 决定提交或回滚后重新规划，并在固定候选池与预算下用更少真实工具调用获得更好指标。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「先预测后果再调用」的世界模型、风险与不确定性排序、verifier 提交–回滚以及区分选择器与候选空间的归因审计，或可供核查 LVR 中 LOOK/STOP 的收益成本权衡与视觉证据筛选，但任务为图像复原，迁移线索尚属推测。
